newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: LUGE-AUSTRIANS RETAIN WORLD TEAM TITLE.
newsitem.headline: LUGE-AUSTRIANS RETAIN WORLD TEAM TITLE.

text.p: The Igls course record was broken 13 times as Austria successfully defended their team title in the world luge championship on Friday.
They collected 145 points on the course which hosted the 1976 Olympic luge events. Germany, with 139, had to be content with silver for the second successive year and Italy took the bronze on 124.
Andrea Tagwerker and Angelika Neuner finished first (40.110 seconds) and second (40.145) respectively in the women's leg, ahead of Italy's Gerda Weissensteiner.
The Austrian double, comprising cousins Tobias and Markus Schiegl, edged out the German pair by just .008 of a second, winning in 40.025.
"When we saw how strong our women were, we knew we could do it," said Tobias Schiegl. "We gave it all because we did not want to be the ones who lost the medal for Austria."

Austria's hopes of a clean sweep in the day's team events were dashed by Germany's Jens Muller, who won the men's leg in 48.833. But they placed second and fourth with Markus Prock (48.934) and Gerhard Gleirscher (49.113) respectively.
"I never thought we would beat the Germans," said delighted Austrian team leader Prock. "They are such a strong team."
The championships continue on Saturday with the women's event. The men compete on Sunday.
